MUQATIL:11:115-117/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:115-117/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:115-117/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to persevere in prayer; God does not waste the reward of those who act with sincerity.

TAB-FULL:v12p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627/r1.claim: God commands Muhammad to endure the harm and hardships inflicted by his people for God's sake, hoping for His great reward; God preserves the reward of every obedient person.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2093/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2093/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2093/r1.claim: An earlier scripture says envy harms only the envier; patience saves the envied person, as God does not waste the reward of those who do good.

THALABI:v5p193/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p193/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to endure the harm he meets; alternative explanations specify patience through harm or in prayer, as in the command to enjoin prayer on one’s family.

THALABI:v5p193/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p193/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains those whose reward God does not waste as people who pray.

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r10.claim: The truly beneficent person knows that reward for patient obedience comes through God’s grace, not through any earned entitlement.

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r9.claim: Patience means embracing what God decrees with a good bearing and leaving what He forbids.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r1.claim: The command to be patient is interpreted as patience in prayer, as in the command to tell one's family to pray and persevere in it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p583/r2.claim: The “doers of good” rewarded by God are those who pray.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r5.claim: Patience here means persistence in prayer, and God does not waste the reward of those who do good, meaning worshippers.

JISHUMI:v5p3579/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r7.claim: Patience may mean persisting in conveying the message and fulfilling people's rights, or enduring the harm caused by unbelievers.

JISHUMI:v5p3579/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r8.claim: God does not nullify the good deeds of those who excel but pays their reward fully; Ibn ʿAbbās identifies them here as those who pray.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r1.claim: The command to be patient is directed to Muhammad amid the harm he faces; another view applies it to prayer, as in 20:132.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r2.claim: God does not waste the reward of those who do good in their deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the good-doers meant here are those who pray.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r3.claim: The sequence says God repays everyone for good and bad deeds, commands steadfastness, promises reward for prayer, then patience in preaching and hardship, and promises not to waste the good-doers' reward.

TABRISI:11:114#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:114#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:114#2/r6.claim: Here patience may mean steadfastness in prayer, as in the command to order one's family to pray and persist in it.

TABRISI:11:115-117/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:115-117/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the reward of the doers of good here as referring to those who pray.

TABRISI:11:115-117/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r2.claim: The command tells Muhammad to endure his people's harm and denial, fulfil obligations, and avoid blameworthy acts; God fully rewards good-doers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r3.claim: The following verse commands patience and assures that God will not waste the reward of those who do good.

RAZI-FULL:v18p59#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p59#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p59#2/r5.claim: Some say the command to be patient refers to prayer, as in 20:132.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.claim: Patience means persistence in prayer, as in the command to make one's household pray and patiently keep at it.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.claim: Another interpretation commands Muhammad to endure the harm he encounters.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.claim: The reward promised to those who do good refers here to people who pray.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r1.claim: Be patient in obedience and in avoiding sins; God will not waste the reward of those who act well, proving that prayer and patience are good deeds and implying the need for sincerity.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.claim: Be patient in carrying out commands and avoiding prohibitions, since none of it can be completed without patience.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#2/r2.claim: From 'remain steadfast' through 'be patient,' and other good deeds, the passage contains all commands and prohibitions.

QASHANI:11:114-115/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r7.claim: Be patient through God in steadfastness and with God in presence during prayer, avoiding reliance on others; God preserves the reward of those who witness while fulfilling justice and reverence.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r4.claim: Be patient in obedience, away from sin, and in continuing to warn; do not fear opponents, since the outcome favors those who obey.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r5.claim: God never wastes the reward of people perfected in worshipful excellence; patience is difficult, but obedience requires it, and religion as a whole is patience.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r6.claim: The author cites the report that Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires, and links the promise to the verse that the patient receive their reward without measure.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r1.claim: Be patient through the hardships of fulfilling what you have been charged to do. Al-Kashshāf says the renewed command highlights patience’s special merit and necessity for obedience and avoiding prohibitions.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r2.claim: Uprightness entails perseverance in speech, action, and belief, hence patience in obedience and avoiding disobedience; another view makes patience continual, like the prayer command in 20:132.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r3.claim: A defense says resisting natural inclination toward tyranny or wrongdoers is difficult; al-Ālūsī replies that natural side effects are not prohibited, as loving one’s unbelieving child is not sinful, and the total burden of duties suffices.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r4.claim: God fully pays those who do good without loss, proving His freedom from depriving them and grounding patience; this patience is ihsān. Muqātil says ihsān is sincerity, Ibn ʿAbbās says those who pray.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#2/r5.claim: Commands to do good are singularly addressed to the Prophet though general in meaning, while prohibitions use the plural for the community, honoring him.

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r16.claim: The Prophet is told to endure the hardship of carrying out these commands and to await help against wrongdoers without impatience, since God never wastes the reward of those who do good.

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r17.claim: This closing patience command reinforces and expands the command in Yūnus 10:109 to follow revelation and be patient.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r1.claim: The command to be patient continues the reassurance against delayed punishment for those who deny.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r2.claim: Patience follows uprightness and avoiding the wrongdoers because these commands are difficult and oppose many people's desires.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r3.claim: The Prophet is addressed as an honor, but the universal reason includes his community; patience is one of the good deeds of the righteous.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p182#2/r4.claim: The reward is called a wage because it is promised as recompense for deeds and therefore resembles payment.

TABATABAI:11:114-116/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r2.claim: Prayer and patience are paired as major pillars of worship and moral life; together they steady a person through hardship by calming distress and turning attention to God.

TABATABAI:11:114-116/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r3.claim: The open-ended command includes obedience, avoiding sin, and enduring adversity; its singular address suggests a special call for the Prophet to bear abuse while inviting people to God.

TABATABAI:11:114-116/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r4.claim: The author supports interpreters who understand the command as patience through the Prophet's people's harm and oppression.

TABATABAI:11:114-116/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r5.claim: The promise that God does not waste the reward of those who do good explains why the Prophet is to remain patient.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r5.claim: Addressing all people through the Prophet, the next verse says those who carry out the commands and prohibitions will meet hardship and should be patient.

STUDYQURAN:11:114/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:114/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:114/r12.claim: The link between patience and God’s reward is discussed in the commentary on 11:11.

STUDYQURAN:11:114/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:114/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:114/r13.claim: Other verses also promise that God will not neglect believers’ reward: 3:171, 7:170, 9:120, 12:56, 12:90, and 18:30.

STUDYQURAN:11:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:intro/r18.speaker: author
